questions.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(-2,{5}^{2}),$ compute $P(X<9).$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,2.0\,$ | $\,0.9772\,$ | $\,0.9778\,$ | $\,0.9783\,$ |
| $\,2.1\,$ | $\,0.9821\,$ | $\,0.9826\,$ | $\,0.9830\,$ |
| $\,2.2\,$ | $\,0.9861\,$ | $\,0.9864\,$ | $\,0.9868\,$ |

$P(X<9)=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(X<x)=P(Z<\frac{x-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =-2$ and $\sigma =5.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<9) & =P(Z<\frac{9-(-2)}{5}) \\  & =P(Z<2.2) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.2) \\  & =Φ(2.2)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/8ac4c36c58d5189e2483a71e2b0dbbe8e629dd9537d90b2338000d36915880a1.png)

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(2.2)=0.9861.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(X<9)=0.9861.
$$

$$
P(Y\ge y)=P(Z\ge \frac{y-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =-2$ and $\sigma =4.$

First, we transform $Y$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge -4.48) & =P(Z\ge \frac{-4.48-(-2)}{4}) \\  & =P(Z\ge -0.62).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(a<X<b)=P(\frac{a-\mu }{\sigma }<Z<\frac{b-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =10$ and $\sigma =4.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(10.64<X<18.28) & =P(\frac{10.64-10}{4}<Z<\frac{18.28-10}{4}) \\  & =P(0.16<Z<2.07).\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/dc1c1e8b01372821c4ad13bfb1bbfd2a102bb9d247815ace25219d3a3f42c8c2.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.16<Z<2.07) & =P(Z<2.07)-P(Z\le 0.16) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.07)-P(Z\le 0.16) \\  & =Φ(2.07)-Φ(0.16).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(2.07) & =0.9808 \\ Φ(0.16) & =0.5636\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.16<Z<2.07) & =Φ(2.07)-Φ(0.16) \\  & =0.9808-0.5636 \\  & =0.4172.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(10.64<X<18.28)=0.4172.
$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $Y \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2),$ we have

$$
P(Y \geq y) = P \left( Z \geq \dfrac{y-\mu}{\sigma} \right)
$$

where $Z \sim N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu = 5$ and $\sigma = 4.$

First, we transform $Y$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge 2.92) & =P(Z\ge \frac{2.92-5}{4}) \\  & =P(Z\ge -0.52)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/049e4733082674668ebbe2c5a710cd847f1db16d26fdcd2af6e603941efdffe7.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $\Phi(z)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -0.52) & =1-P(Z<-0.52) \\  & =1-P(Z\le -0.52) \\  & =1-Φ(-0.52)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
\Phi(-0.52) =0.3015.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -0.52) & =1-Φ(-0.52) \\  & =1-0.3015 \\  & =0.6985.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(Y \geq 2.92) = 0.6985.
$$
